summary: The audit checks 135 units of graduate work, every course letter graded when a letter grade is offered: the five MATSCI core courses, eight technical electives for 24 units (five MATSCI courses counting a characterization course, or four plus an outside characterization course, then STEM electives), MATSCI 230 colloquia, 75 units of MATSCI 300 research, and 18 residency units. Checked by hand: STEM electives outside the lists, the 3.0 GPA, taking a course that counts each quarter, safety training, every form and milestone, the qualifying exam, the oral defense and the dissertation. Up to 45 units from an outside MS may transfer with approval.

program.why: Grading: "Any course that satisfies the PhD degree requirements must be taken for a letter grade, if offered."

lwBkZjiT.why: "15 units required." Notes: "All five courses must be taken during the first year and for a letter grade."

tROdezLx.why: "24 total units required." "All technical elective courses must be completed for a letter grade." "Of the eight technical elective courses (24 units), five must be Materials Science and Engineering courses (15 units), and include at least one characterization course (3 units)." "If the characterization course requirement is fulfilled with a MATSCI subject code course, only four additional MATSCI electives are required within the total eight courses." Elective courses "may not include colloquium, research, seminars, or independent study such as MATSCI 200, 230, 231, 232, 299, 300, 399, or 400." "Technical electives outside of the MATSCI electives must be letter-graded graduate lecture/lab courses at the 200 level or above in science fields ... may be approved by the student's advisor and Student Services." The two characterization cases are two paths; the outside electives name no subject codes and are moved in by hand. MATSCI 402A and 402T (1-unit topics seminars offered only satisfactory/no credit) are left out of the MATSCI electives too: "Elective courses must be taken for a letter grade and may not include colloquium, research, seminars".
